laws.title: The cheap-click headline formula: specific price + specific timeframe + implied story
laws.actionable: Use for reach and traffic goals only, never as a lead-quality signal.
laws.evidence: 'Someone Bought This Robina Home Six Months Ago' $0.16/click, 946 clicks, $152.96 · 'The Owner Paid $475,000 in 2010. They're Now Asking $1,285,000' $0.31/click, 111 clicks · '$1,710,000 on Outrigger Drive' $0.14/click, 92 clicks · 'Who buys for $1,550,000 and sells eighteen months later for $3,465,000?' $0.12/click, 48 clicks.

laws.title: Broad market commentary without a personal stake gets the most expensive clicks
laws.actionable: Never ship a suburb-statistic headline with no personal stake.
laws.evidence: 'Robina's Fastest-Moving Year in Half a Decade' $7.29/click (copy) and $5.10/click (original), 8 clicks total, ~$56 spent · 'Southern Gold Coast Apartment Boom' $5.83/click, 6 clicks · 'Gold Coast Interstate Migration' $2.02/click, 6 clicks · 'Robina Sales Volume Surges 111%' $3.31/click, 2 clicks. Against $0.12-$0.31 for story formats. Independently corroborated by the hook corpus: the same 'Fastest-Moving Year' ad is the WORST performer above the evidence floor at 0.05% CTR on 1,879 impressions.

laws.title: Abstract concepts die at scroll speed — 7 of 7, zero exceptions
laws.actionable: Show the number. Never name the category the number is in.
laws.evidence: AN6 'five-figure gap' 0.6% CTR / 151 impressions · AN8 'a different number' 2.4% / 247 · AN12 visual info-gap 0.00% / 76 · AN20 'wrong year' 0.9% / 106 · AN22 net proceeds 2.81% / 178 · AN23 three numbers 2.99% / 167 · AN25 equity 3.68% / 190. Contrast AN2's concrete '$1,440,000 → $2,500,000' at 9.44% CTR.

laws.title: A dollar anchor is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT — one number, not a puzzle
laws.actionable: One number per hook. Never a spread, never a three-way framework.
laws.evidence: AN39 'The Valuation Spread' (three appraisals $1.2M/$1.35M/$1.48M → a $280,000 spread): 0 link clicks on 114 combined impressions, 0.00% CTR both backgrounds, AFTER a starvation-relief cull guaranteed a fair auction for a full hour. AN40 'Kitchen Math' ($80,000 kitchen returns ~$34,000): dark 0.0% on 69 impressions, light 1.4% on 71 — the second kill of the renovation axis after AN13's narrative-only death.

laws.title: Aggregate statistics create awareness; single specific examples create identification
laws.evidence: AN1 raw stat 2.4% CTR / 295 impressions / $21.71 / 0 leads · AN4 same stat plus an address ask 1.4% / 155 · AN24 same stat as a research narrative, dark 3.92% / 102, light 3.03% / 99. Six variants, ~900 impressions, zero leads.

laws.title: Scroll depth from Facebook traffic caps at ~50% regardless of content quality
laws.actionable: Put anything that must be seen above the halfway point of the page.
laws.evidence: Three separate tests, ~1,200 total sessions, identical result: V2 broad 50.1%, V2 core 50.3%, V3 49.8% — average and median both ~50%, unchanged by content improvements that lifted time on page +24%.

laws.title: Only 10% of feed visitors reach the CTA — it sits below the scroll ceiling
laws.evidence: V3 section funnel: feed view 86% → Seller Anchor 38% (a 48pp drop) → Big Mistake 32% → Insight 30% → Compare 24% → Fields Pick 15% → Save Worthy 14% → Seller Bridge 13% → CTA 10%.

laws.title: Article pages are dead ends — 95% read and leave; zero property views from any ad
laws.actionable: A new hook cannot fix this. Do not attribute a conversion failure to the headline until a next step exists.
laws.evidence: Of 310 tracked Facebook sessions: 296 stayed on the article page only, 2 reached /for-sale, 1 reached a property page, 11 reached market-intelligence. And: zero tracked property views across ALL ads in the attribution data.

cautions.title: The semantic hook corpus contains ZERO lead-optimised ads — CTR is all it can measure
cautions.actionable: Annotating the 108 OUTCOME_LEADS ads is the single highest-value unblock — it would let the hook taxonomy be tested against leads rather than clicks.
cautions.evidence: Join of ad_profiles (203) to ad_semantic_annotations (92) matches 92 of 92 on ad_id. Objective mix of the matched set: OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT 57 ads / 74,649 impressions · OUTCOME_TRAFFIC 33 / 217,956 · OUTCOME_AWARENESS 2 / 12,603. The account's 108 OUTCOME_LEADS ads — including all 43 homeowner-funnel angles — are entirely UNANNOTATED. Attributed leads in the corpus: 0. Only 55 of 92 rows clear a 500-impression evidence floor.

cautions.title: READ FIRST — the entire copy-discovery run rests on 7 lead events
cautions.actionable: The prescribed fix was to move the optimisation target up-funnel to engagement, where there are 50-100x the data points per dollar.
cautions.evidence: Verbatim from the mandate scoping doc: '$868 spend → 7 leads → 4 quality "Yes" (one of those a fake +93 phone). Blended CPL $124. The killer problem is reward sparsity. 1-2 leads per winning ad is statistically noise. You cannot optimise copy — let alone sequences of copy — on 7 events. Every cycle "verdict" to date is a coin-flip dressed as a finding. All conversions landed Day 1, then flatlined despite continued spend — but off 1-2 leads that decay is indistinguishable from noise.'

cautions.title: All copy testing ran OUT OF MARKET — funnel shape transfers, economics do not
cautions.actionable: Never quote a funnel-run CPL as a Gold Coast forecast.
cautions.evidence: Verbatim: 'Transfers to GC: funnel SHAPE, PII-resistance RANKING, warm-up DEPTH, hook MECHANICS — these are structural/psychological. Does NOT transfer: absolute CPL, absolute conversion rate, whether the person is a real prospect (Brisbane people aren't your buyers). Economics are re-validated only in a GC run — never trust a Brisbane CPL as a GC forecast.' Out-of-market leads received nothing post-submit by design.

dead_hook_mechanics.mechanic: Naming the category instead of showing the number
dead_hook_mechanics.detail: 'a five-figure gap', 'the valuation spread', 'the equity you can't see'. The abstraction is the failure, not the topic.

dead_hook_mechanics.mechanic: A population statistic offered as if it were personal
dead_hook_mechanics.detail: '89% of homes are overvalued', '3.6% national growth'. Aggregates create awareness, never identification. One specific address outperforms every time.

dead_hook_mechanics.mechanic: Pure utility with no open question
dead_hook_mechanics.detail: 'Sold-price alerts', 'The Cost of Selling — itemised'. Useful, complete, and therefore nothing to click. A headline that answers itself has no reader.

dead_hook_mechanics.mechanic: More than one number in the hook
dead_hook_mechanics.detail: Three-figure frameworks and spreads compete with themselves. One dominant number per headline. A second number belongs in the body.

dead_hook_mechanics.mechanic: Generic 'how to' / 'is now a good time' framing
dead_hook_mechanics.detail: Confirmed on our OWN articles, not just ads — see the headline table.
